Article Title: Greg Chappell leads seven Australia captains in appeal to foreign minister over 'humanitarian' Imran Khan concerns
Article Text:
Imran Khan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Mumbai: Former Australia captain and India head coach Greg Chappell has stepped up his efforts to secure fair medical treatment and welfare for former Pakistan Prime Minister and 1992 World Cup-winning captain Imran Khan.As part of Chappell's latest initiative, seven former Australia captains have approached Foreign Minister Penny Wong over humanitarian concerns surrounding Imran's detention in Pakistan. They have urged the Australian Government to raise the matter directly with the relevant Pakistani authorities.The letter, a copy of which is with TOI, was signed by Allan Border, Greg Chappell, Ian Chappell, Belinda Clark, Kim Hughes, Mark Taylor and Steve Waugh. They stressed that they were writing "not as diplomats or political actors, but as former Australian captains who felt we should speak up."The group said it was taking no position on the legal or political case against Imran, which it described as a matter for Pakistan. Their concern, they said, was the treatment of anyone in detention, calling it “a matter of basic humanity, whatever their politics.”The former captains highlighted concerns raised publicly by Imran's sons and sisters over his health and treatment, including limited medical care, restricted family contact and minimal access to legal counsel.The letter also referred to Chappell's last meeting with Imran in Islamabad in 2022, when he was Pakistan's prime minister and, according to Chappell, "hale, hearty and fit.""Greg Chappell last saw Imran Khan in Islamabad in 2022, when Khan was Prime Minister — hale, hearty and fit, by his account. It is hard to reconcile that image with the reports now coming out of his detention, and that is why we write to you today, not as diplomats or political actors, but as former Australian captains who felt we should speak up. Khan led Pakistan to its only World Cup title. He also led his country as Prime Minister. Australians hold him in great regard — as a cricketer whose skill and leadership left a lasting mark on the game we share, and as someone who has helped improve the lives of Pakistanis by building cancer hospitals.""Beyond credible reports, his own sons and sisters have been pleading publicly for months over his health and treatment in detention — limited medical care, restricted family contact, and minimal access to legal counsel among their concerns."The letter concluded: "This is not the first time international captains have raised this concern. It has been brought to public attention on two separate occasions in the past six months, and the reports since then — now echoed by his own family — suggest the situation has not improved. We would be grateful if the Australian Government could raise this directly with the relevant Pakistani authorities. Mr Chappell has also requested a meeting with you on this matter over recent weeks, and would welcome the chance to discuss it with you directly on our behalf. Thank you for taking the time to consider this."The appeal comes weeks after 21 former international captains from nine cricketing nations, including India's Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev and Dilip Vengsarkar, wrote to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Aug 23 over Imran's medical treatment and welfare.That letter, a follow-up to one signed by 14 former captains in February, followed developments that the group said fell short of a Supreme Court directive on Imran's treatment. The court had ordered that Khan be transferred to hospital for examination by a medical board including his own physicians and his sister, Dr Uzma Khan, alongside reinstated weekly family visits.The 73-year-old Imran has been in jail for more than three years following his tenure as Pakistan's prime minister and is currently facing severe health issues.Since the first letter, Imran's former Pakistan teammates, including a tearful Javed Miandad, Wasim Akram and Moin Khan, have spoken out, as has current Australia captain Pat Cummins.Chappell had also requested a meeting with Wong last month to discuss the matter on behalf of the group but has yet to receive a response.
Article Summary: Seven former Australia captains have approached Foreign Minister Penny Wong over humanitarian concerns surrounding Imran's detention in Pakistan. They have urged the Australian Government to raise the matter directly with the relevant Pakistani authorities. They stressed that they were writing "not as diplomats or political actors, but as former Australian captains who felt we should speak up" The group said it was taking no position on the legal or political case against Imran, which it described as a matter for Pakistan.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: 'The mistakes I made, I won't make again' - Sprinter Animesh Kujur ready for a bigger challenge
Article Text:
Animesh Kujur (Image credit: Special arrangement)

Animesh Kujur (Image credit: Special arrangement)

A tougher sprint field awaits in Aichi-Nagoya

The clock is no longer driving Kujur's races

Animesh Kujur won bronze medal in 200m at 2025 Asian Championships (Image credit: Special arrangement)

The lessons from his first international campaign

Learning when to push - and when to back off

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Animesh Kujur with Martin Owens (Image credit: Special arrangement)

‘I know I am going to do well’

By the time Animesh Kujur lined up for the 200m at the Indian Athletics Series Final at the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Delhi last week, the instruction from his coach was fairly simple: don't chase the clock.It was getting late. The priority was to stay injury-free, execute the bend and finish the race.Kujur won in 20.59 seconds after winning the 100m in 10.21 seconds. Gurindervir Singh, India's 100m national record holder, was second in 10.32.The meeting was the final domestic stop before the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. For Kujur, the two victories were less about producing another headline time than getting through the evening and into the final phase of his preparation.“The coach said that the time is getting late, so just stay injury-free. Don't push too much. Just try to come first,” Kujur told TimesofIndia.com after the race. “Just try to execute the curve. That's it. And I just did it like that. I came straight and just maintained my pace. And just finished the race.”He arrives in Aichi-Nagoya with a 10.14 personal best in the 100m and the national 200m record of 20.32, set at the 2025 Asian Championships.He will compete in the 100m, 200m and relay.The 10.14 came in Wetzlar, Germany, in July and remains the second-fastest 100m by an Indian, behind Gurindervir's 10.09 national record. Kujur's run was also the fastest 100m by an Indian outside the country.Gurindervir's 10.09 came at the Federation Cup in Ranchi in May, when the Indian record changed hands repeatedly over a short period. Kujur had run 10.15 before Gurindervir reclaimed the record with 10.09.The two have continued to race each other through the season. At the Series Final in Delhi, Kujur had the better of the two again.Kujur said that competition has changed the way he feels about the 100m.“I will say 100, I am having more fun now because I am getting competition from Guri again and again,” he said.He does not feel the same level of competition in the 200m.“In 200, there is not as much competition as there should be in India,” he said. “But when you get competition, that is when you enjoy running fast.”The Asian Games will give him plenty of it.Japan's Shuhei Tada and Yuki Koike are listed for the men's 100m. Tada has a 10.01 personal best, while Koike has run 10.06. Both are part of Japan's Asian Games sprint team.The wider Asian field has also produced several sub-10.10-level performances this season, with Japan's Rikuto Higuchi at 10.01 and other Japanese sprinters around the 10.03-10.04 mark. Gurindervir's 10.09 and Kujur's 10.14 put the Indian pair firmly in that group.The 200m is an even tougher proposition on paper.Japan's Soshi Mizukubo has run 20.07 this season and won the Japanese national title. Thailand's Puripol Boonson has gone 20.03, a national record, while Kujur's Indian record remains 20.32.Kujur's own 2026 200m season has been less spectacular than his record-breaking 2025, but that has not altered how he sees the event.Earlier in the year, he qualified for the Asian Games with 20.74 at the National Inter-State Championships, a time comfortably inside the qualification mark but well outside his 20.32 national record.He has since been thinking less about producing a particular time in every race.In 2024, Kujur said, he spent an entire season running around 20.5 and 20.6. Then came 20.40 at the Senior Federation Cup in 2025, followed by 20.32 at the Asian Championships.“So when it has to happen, it will happen,” he said. “No matter how much you push, the conditions should be like that, competition should be like that, and the atmosphere should be like that. And it's all about that day.”There is a similar change in his 100m target.The conversation around Kujur had once centred on whether he could break 10 seconds. Kujur has moved his own target further.“No, I don't think of 10 flat, now I think of running 9,” he said.Even after running 10.21, he felt there was more there.“Even today, when I stood in 10.16, I thought, this is not a 10.16 race,” he said. “So it's okay, when it has to come, it comes.”What matters now is getting the body to the right point. Kujur's first major international experience came at the 2025 Asian Championships, where he won bronze in the 200m. He says he was under pressure because he was representing India officially for the first time.He does not expect that feeling to return in Japan.“And the mistakes I made in the Asian Championships, I won't make again,” he said. “Because I was first international. Officially, I was representing India. And I was under pressure for that.”Since then, he has raced at the World Championships, on the Continental Tour and at other international competitions. His coach has also encouraged him to use those races to experiment.“With the upcoming LA Olympics, [the coaches have told me] don't miss any chance to make a mistake. And our ultimate aim is the LA Olympics,” Kujur said.The Asian Games therefore arrive after a season in which Kujur has learned more about managing the work around the races.That will be particularly relevant in Aichi-Nagoya. Kujur says the heat and humidity will not be new to him.“Yes, it is the same condition where I train. Same humidity, same heat,” he said. “And last time I competed in the World Championship. So I have an idea how to keep my body there and how to maintain things.”“I know what form I am in, how my body is behaving, what time to take my body, when to peak, when to reduce the load, all the things that we have learned from the last year, how to maintain everything,” he said.There is also a sizeable support system behind Kujur's preparation.“I have a lot of people on my support, like Reliance, Odisha Government, then TOPS, Athletic Federation of India, and others, and Puma, they never let me down,” he said. “Everyone wants me to improve, in every field, whether it's performance wise, or mental peace, or anything else. As a normal human being, everyone wants me to improve.”The expectation he carries into his first Asian Games is also different from the one he had at the Asian Championships.He has already won an Asian medal. He now wants to win one at a bigger multi-sport event.“The success of the Asian Games will be a life-changing moment for me, because I have never won a medal in such a big game,” he said.Asked which of the 100m, 200m and relay he considered his best medal opportunity, he did not pick one.“Sure shot medal,” Kujur said. “I have won all three.”
Article Summary: Animesh Kujur will compete in the 100m, 200m and relay at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. He arrives with a 10.14 personal best in the100m and the national 200m record of 20.32, set at the 2025 Asian Championships. The 2026 Games are his first international campaign.

Article Title: Mohsin Naqvi 'didn't object' to India refusing Women's Asia Cup trophy from him, says Rajeev Shukla
Article Text:
India beat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Asia Cup final in Dubai on Sunday, but the team did not accept the trophy from Naqvi

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla on Monday said the Indian women's team's decision not to receive the Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) chairman Mohsin Naqvi was taken collectively by the Board, adding that Naqvi "did not raise any objection" to it.India beat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Asia Cup final in Dubai on Sunday, but the team did not accept the trophy from Naqvi. It was the second year in a row that an Indian team skipped receiving the Asia Cup trophy from the ACC chairman, after the men's team did the same during the 2025 Asia Cup following the Pahalgam terror attack.“We discussed the matter among ourselves and decided that we would not accept it (trophy) from him. It was our collective decision. He (Naqvi) also did not raise any objection to it,” Shukla told reporters after arriving with the team at the Indira Gandhi International Airport.“We informed our team accordingly, and he presented it to whoever he had to and then left,” Shukla added, as quoted by news agency PTI.Shukla's comments were in line with BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia's explanation after the final.Saikia had said the Board's stand changed after the 2025 Pahalgam terror attack, while adding that India would continue to play Pakistan in multinational tournaments in line with the government's policy.“Our men’s team won the Asia Cup a year and a half ago. And our whole situation, since the April 2025 Pahalgam incident, changed after that. So, after that, there was pressure on us from our citizens that we shouldn’t keep any relations with our neighboring country and not play cricket with them. But our government has a policy that we must play against every country in multinational tournaments,” Saikia had told IANS.“But that doesn’t mean we will follow every condition laid out for us. Our military conflict is still ongoing. One of the main leaders who is working against the interests of our country; we can’t receive the trophy from him. The Women’s team has expressed solidarity with the decision taken by the men’s team last year,” Saikia had said.Earlier, pictures had surfaced showing Saikia talking to Naqvi during the Asia Cup final in Dubai. Responding to the criticism over those images, Shukla said it was only a professional interaction during the match.“What Saikia ji said is absolutely correct. When you are at a match, everyone is present there and interacts in a professional capacity. Therefore, I do not think there should be so much criticism over that,” he said.
Article Summary: India beat Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the Asia Cup final in Dubai on Sunday. But the team did not accept the trophy from Mohsin Naqvi. It was the second year in a row that an Indian team skipped receiving the trophy. The men's team did the same during the 2025 Asia Cup.

Article Title: Pat Cummins warns Australia could face 'hostility' on first South Africa Test tour since Sandpaper Gate
Article Text:
Pat Cummins, Steve Smith and Marnus Labuschagne

Cummins expects some hostility in South Africa

'Everyone moves on', says Australian captain

Cummins rejects preparation excuse after Bangladesh loss

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Australia captain Pat Cummins expects the Test team could encounter some hostility when it returns to South Africa for its first red-ball tour there since the infamous Sandpaper Gate scandal of 2018.Australia are scheduled to play three ODIs and three Tests in South Africa. Although the Australians have continued to visit the country for white-ball cricket since the ball-tampering controversy, the upcoming Test series will mark their first in South Africa since the incident.Cummins is currently not with Australia for the three-match ODI series in Zimbabwe but will link up with the squad in South Africa for the one-dayers before the Test campaign begins on October 9.Speaking on the Keepin’ it Cricket podcast, Cummins acknowledged that the 2018 episode could still be brought up by sections of the home support."There might be a little bit of hostility," Cummins admitted. "(But) it can't be louder than an Ashes series … Birmingham, the Hollies Stand at Edgbaston, that gets pretty rowdy."The Australian skipper has already experienced South African crowds during previous white-ball tours and was also one of the standout performers during Australia's 2018 Test series against the Proteas.He does not expect anything completely unfamiliar when Australia return for the three-Test contest."As long as I've been to South Africa, there are some parts of the crowd that get stuck in, but I reckon we've seen it all before."And most importantly, I'm captain, so I'm in the middle; I'm not near the fence!"Cummins also suggested that the reaction to Sandpaper Gate may not be as intense as some might expect. He recalled that the issue had been heavily discussed during previous encounters but felt the response from South African fans was ultimately less dramatic than anticipated."It (Sandpapergate) was kind of really spoken up (in past series), and it was almost a bit underwhelming," Cummins said about the reaction from Proteas fans.For Cummins, the best way to move beyond the controversy will be to focus on the cricket once the series gets underway."Everyone moves on. The good thing is, three Tests, you get stuck into the cricket, and everyone just worries about the cricket pretty quickly."I'm sure there'll be some rowdy people in the crowd, and some articles or some media bring up stuff. But our group's moved on," he added.Australia still have six players in their current setup who were part of the squad that lost the 2018 series 1-3 to South Africa. The tour became one of the darkest episodes in Australian cricket after the ball-tampering scandal led to year-long bans for Steve Smith and David Warner , while Cameron Bancroft was suspended for nine months.Cummins also reflected on Australia's recent defeat to Bangladesh in Darwin, their first home loss to the Bangla Tigers.The result prompted questions over whether Australia had been adequately prepared for the series, but Cummins dismissed that suggestion."Whether that was an Ashes Test or a Bangladesh series, I think we would have prepped exactly the same. Of course you look at it after the series, but I actually thought we were in a really good spot; everyone fit, firing."The Australian captain accepted, however, that his side simply failed to perform at the required level in Darwin."I just don’t think we played very well. I don’t think it was a lack of prep. I just don’t think we were at our best, and Bangladesh played brilliantly, and didn’t really let us in," he added.
Article Summary: Cummins expects some hostility in South Africa. 'Everyone moves on', says Australian captain Pat Cummins. Australia are scheduled to play three ODIs and three Tests in the country. Australia lost the 2018 series 1-3 to South Africa after the ball-tampering scandal.

Article Title: “You will inspire many more”: How Sophie Cunningham left a young Fever fan in tears with one unforgettable gesture after Indiana’s win
Article Text:
How Sophie Cunningham left a young Fever fan in tears with one unforgettable gesture after Indiana’s win(Getty)

Sophie Cunningham noticed a young fan and gave her a game-worn shoe after the Fever’s 112-98 win

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Sophie Cunningham had already played her part in the Indiana Fever’s 112-98 win over the Portland Fire on Friday, August 1, 2026. But the moment that stayed with fans came after the final buzzer. Cunningham walked toward a young Fever supporter in the stands and handed her one of her game-worn shoes. The girl looked stunned, then covered her face as the emotion hit her.The Indiana Fever later shared the moment on social media, and the young fan’s reaction quickly drew attention. She did not simply take the shoe and move on. She looked at it in disbelief before becoming visibly emotional. For Cunningham, it was a quick postgame gesture. For the young supporter, it became a memory tied to a Fever win she will likely never forget.The moment came at the end of a busy night for Cunningham in Portland. She had dealt with boos from sections of the Moda Center crowd when she entered the game midway through the first quarter. Rather than let the reception affect her, she answered with a three-pointer and finished with 13 points as Indiana picked up its fifth straight victory.Then came the part nobody could have planned. After the final buzzer, Cunningham walked toward the stands and handed a young Fever fan her game-worn shoe. The child immediately looked overwhelmed. In the video shared by the Fever on August 1, she appeared to stare at the shoe in disbelief before putting her hands over her face.The Fever highlighted that exact reaction in its social media post, writing, “The reaction on this young fan’s face when Sophie Cunningham gifted her a game-worn shoe after tonight’s win in Portland.”It was a fitting way to end a night that had already given Fever fans plenty to celebrate. Indiana scored 112 points, with Caitlin Clark leading the way with 26 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists. Kelsey Mitchell also scored 26, while the Fever pulled away with a 34-point third quarter. The victory marked Indiana’s fifth consecutive win, and the team became the first in WNBA history to score at least 100 points in five straight games.But the young fan’s reaction shifted the focus from the scoreboard to something much more personal.Fever fans praised Sophie Cunningham for giving the young supporter a memory she will never forgetThe reaction did not stop with the video. Fans flooded the Fever’s post with messages praising Cunningham for taking the time to connect with a young supporter.One fan wrote, “How beautiful is this amazing woman, inside and out! She's Phenominal!!”Another folk added, “You will be remembered for being on the right side of history @sophaller.”One fan even admitted that Cunningham had changed their feelings about the Fever, writing, “I usually only root for New York teams, but @sophaller has made me a fan of the Indiana Fever, simply because she’s an amazing person, God Bless!”Another fan thanked Cunningham for the way she interacts with supporters, writing, “Thank you Sophie for always standing up for what is right and being there for the fans. I wish more athletes had your strength and moral courage.You will inspire many more.”There was also a lighter reaction to the postgame interaction. One fan joked about Cunningham using her long reach for a selfie, writing, “Sophie's like ‘obviously we'll use my extra-long arms to take a selfie’ 🤣 She's a gem.”Cunningham’s shoe may have been just another piece of equipment after a WNBA game. For the young Fever fan, though, it became something much bigger. She left Portland with a game-worn souvenir, a special interaction with Sophie Cunningham and a story that started with a 112-98 Indiana victory.
Article Summary: Sophie Cunningham gave a young Fever fan a game-worn shoe after the Fever’s 112-98 win over the Portland Fire on Friday, August 1, 2026. The girl looked stunned, then covered her face as the emotion hit her. The Indiana Fever later shared the moment on social media.

Article Title: From Glasgow setback to Nagoya challenge, Pranati Nayak aims to get it right this time at Asian Games
Article Text:
Pranati Nayak with coach Ashok Mishra

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: When Pranati Nayak gets ready to sprint down the runway at Nagoya City General Gymnasium during the Asian Games later this month, the memory of Glasgow will inevitably return.At the Commonwealth Games, a lack of speed in her approach disrupted her first vault in the qualifying round, costing her valuable points and, ultimately, a place in the final.It was obviously not something one is used to seeing from Nayak and even left her long-time coach Ashok Mishra at a loss for words. “It was the first time I had seen her miss the running,” said Mishra.He, however, downplayed concerns over her injury, insisting that it was not what cost her in Glasgow. She had been dealing with plantar fasciitis — a problem underneath the foot that caused some pulling while running — but had competed with it before and even won a medal this year.Despite that, coach Mishra didn’t want to take any risks and made sure she got enough rest to prepare for her fourth Asian Games appearance, where she will compete only in the vault.“It is around 90-95% cured. Just 5% remains, and that is not a problem for her,” added Mishra.“After the Commonwealth Games, I gave her around three weeks of complete rest. So, she recovered. Otherwise, if we had continued training, it could have aggravated the injury.”But more importantly, the time helped her heal mentally.“She is now mentally much more mature. After everything, we just analyse it and focus on the next,” said Mishra. Also helping her stay focused are psychologists who not only talk to her but also help her with concentration exercises.Irrespective of that, one cannot deny that age is not on her side anymore and that it does make things difficult for the 31-year-old. Still, coach Mishra is confident that Nayak is all set for the challenge.That confidence is rooted in what Nayak has achieved since contemplating walking away from the sport after the Tokyo Olympics in 2021. She has since won two Asian Championship medals, two World Cup medals and one World Challenge Cup medal for India — a run that explains why Mishra still believes she has earned her place among the country’s best.But there is no doubt that the competition will be fierce at the Asian Games.China, Japan, North and South Korea and Chinese Taipei are among the leading gymnastics nations in the continent, while countries such as Philippines and Malaysia have also strengthened their programmes. The Korean gymnasts, in particular, are expected to pose a major challenge on vault.“It’s going to be a very difficult test for her. But I think she will do well. If she does both the 360-degree twist vaults cleanly with a fixed landing, then there is a very good possibility of her going to the final because execution matters,” said Mishra.Keeping this in mind, the coach has centred her training on reducing executional errors and improving explosive strength. To make sure she can do that, Nayak has been working on plyometrics, explosive leg-strength exercises and isometric muscle contractions.She has also been training on soft-landing equipment and in the foam pit, where the physical impact is reduced, before making the transition to the main landing area.For Mishra, that transition is as much mental as physical. “When it comes to the main landing area, it is much more difficult psychologically. You think about how heavy the impact will be,” he said.Nayak certainly has enough experience to make that shift at the right moment. After all, she remains India’s lone gymnast at the Asian Games for the second time in a row. And when she makes that run in Nagoya, the objective will be simple: get the approach right, execute the vault cleanly and, this time, make it to the final.
Article Summary: At the Commonwealth Games, a lack of speed in her approach disrupted her first vault in the qualifying round, costing her valuable points and, ultimately, a place in the final. She had been dealing with plantar fasciitis but had competed with it before and even won a medal this year.

What the Lakers gain from this move

What the Pacers get in return

Dalton Knecht's Lakers career is running out of runway before camp even opens. Los Angeles carries 16 players on guaranteed deals, one over the roster limit, and Knecht, the No. 17 pick in 2024, produced a negative VORP across 553 minutes last season. Heavy.com's Alder Almo has floated sending Knecht and Jarred Vanderbilt to Indiana for Aaron Nesmith, whose $40 million contract and two-way motor fit the timeline L.A. is building around Luka Doncic. Nothing is finalized, and the front office has chased this kind of upgrade all summer without closing a deal.Heavy.com's Alder Almo has proposed routing Knecht and Jarred Vanderbilt to Indiana for Aaron Nesmith, a high-effort piece the Lakers wanted when they pursued Jonathan Kuminga and missed.Almo's proposed framework sends Knecht and Jarred Vanderbilt to Indiana along with a 2032 first-round pick swap, with Nesmith coming back to Los Angeles. Nesmith carries a $40 million contract with the Pacers and brings the kind of relentless, role-flexible energy the Lakers have been shopping for since missing on Kuminga.The Lakers need a starting-caliber wing who can defend and space the floor, and Nesmith checks both boxes without requiring a ball-dominant role next to Doncic.For Indiana, absorbing two young, inexpensive pieces plus a future first-round swap gives them assets to work with even if neither Knecht nor Vanderbilt projects as an immediate rotation fixture.Knecht is entering his third season without having carved out a role. The 6-foot-6 forward out of Tennessee, who finished his senior year fifth in the NCAA in scoring, was the Lakers' 2024 first-round pick, but he barely played last season and posted a negative value over the replacement-player mark.Lake Show Life's Tyler Watts has covered the roster crunch closely. "Knecht is the most likely player to be cut," Watts wrote, adding that the pressure on him during camp is real because the front office hasn't found a trade all offseason. Knecht's game, built around shooting and floor spacing, hasn't matched what the Lakers need defensively next to Doncic and Reaves, and younger, cheaper options like Bronny James and Jaden Hardy give the front office alternatives if they choose to cut rather than trade him.NBA reporter Evan Sidery reported early momentum on this front. "The Lakers are actively shopping Dalton Knecht and Jarred Vanderbilt in trade talks," Sidery wrote.Bleacher Report's Jake Fischer has since confirmed the search is still active. "The Lakers are incomplete right now moving forward," Fischer said, noting there's no urgency to force a deal but that L.A. still wants an upgrade at forward after missing on Kuminga.Hypothetical trade structureNesmith gives the Lakers a plug-and-play forward who can defend multiple positions and space the floor around Doncic and Reaves, exactly the profile they wanted when they pursued Kuminga.Landing him also solves two problems at once: it clears both Knecht and Vanderbilt off the guaranteed-contract list, taking L.A. from 16 down to the required 15 without needing to cut anyone outright.Indiana walks away with two young, inexpensive rotation pieces in Knecht and Vanderbilt, plus a future first-round pick swap in 2032 that adds long-term asset value. Neither player projects as an immediate starter for the Pacers, but the combination gives them flexibility to keep developing or flip the pieces again down the line.
Article Summary: Dalton Knecht's Lakers career is running out of runway before camp even opens. Los Angeles carries 16 players on guaranteed deals, one over the roster limit. The Lakers need a starting-caliber wing who can defend and space the floor. Nesmith checks both boxes without requiring a ball-dominant role.

Article Title: 'I don't cry for my real life': Smriti Mandhana's reply when asked when she last cried
Article Text:
Smriti Mandhana (AFP Photo)

Smriti Mandhana asked about the last time she cried

'Smriti sometimes tries to be Shafali'

Razdan's big expectation from Mandhana

NEW DELHI: India women's cricket team vice-captain Smriti Mandhana is one of the biggest names in women's cricket. Over the years, she has become one of the key players for India and has inspired many young cricketers with her batting and leadership.However, while her cricket career has continued to grow, Mandhana has also gone through a difficult phase in her personal life. Her marriage was called off last year.Mandhana has not spoken publicly about Palash Muchhal , the man she was supposed to marry. During a recent podcast with Shamani, she was asked about the hardest night of her life.Mandhana took a long pause before making it clear that she wanted to speak only about cricket.During the conversation, Shamani asked Mandhana a direct question."When was the last time you cried??" Shamani asked.Mandhana appeared emotional and paused for several seconds before answering the question."Good question. I don't remember. You know, I cry for movies. I don't cry for my real life," Mandhana said.The India star then spoke about a movie that made her emotional."If I watch a movie, I cry. So I think I was watching Mosafir Cafe and it just got me emotional, happy emotional.And I cried," she said.Mandhana then explained why the movie made her emotional."It was very nice. Not even. I got very happy emotion. I was like, yeah, man. I also want to do something like just leave everything, just," she said.Mandhana has largely stayed away from discussing her personal life in public after her marriage was called off.Even during the podcast, she chose to keep the conversation focused on her cricket journey when asked about the difficult period in her life.The India opener now faces another big challenge as India take on Sri Lanka in the Women's Asia Cup final in Dubai.Former India men's cricketer Vivek Razdan believes Mandhana will be one of the most important players for India in the final.India enter Sunday's final as favourites, but defending champions Sri Lanka cannot be taken lightly after their comeback win over Pakistan in the semifinal."The Indian team is a very strong team. But you can't underestimate Sri Lanka, especially the way they played against Pakistan. After being 33/4, they chased down the required target. Despite Athapaththu being out early, you can see how much batting depth the team has," Razdan told IANS in a virtual interaction organised by Sony Sports Network.Razdan also praised India's bowling attack, which has played an important role in the tournament. He, however, wants Mandhana to focus on her own strengths instead of trying to match the aggressive approach of Shafali Verma.Shafali and Mandhana have been India's main run-scorers in the tournament so far, with 168 and 154 runs respectively.Razdan said India need to improve their batting in the powerplay and highlighted the importance of Mandhana staying at the crease for a long time."The Indian team bowling line-up is very strong. You can talk about N Sree Charni, Shafali, or Deepti. All of them have been very strong in these games. But there is one thing that needs to be worked on - how do you bat in powerplay?"In the last game, Shafali scored a fifty against Bangladesh, but she survived three dropped catches and one run-out chance. Regarding Smriti Mandhana, it is very important for her to play for a long time. I don't know why, but I feel that Smriti sometimes tries to be Shafali. That's not her game."Razdan believes India can put up a big total if the top order avoids losing wickets early.With India's middle and lower order capable of finishing strongly, he feels Mandhana's role at the top could prove decisive on Dubai's slow pitches."If you can play the powerplay without losing a wicket, you will be able to post a big score because all of this depends on the top four. We have some batters who can help you at the back end. But if you want to win the match and the final, I will have a special eye on someone to do it, and it will be Smriti Mandhana."
Article Summary: Vivek Razdan wants Smriti Mandhana to play her natural game. Former India men's cricketer says India need to improve batting in powerplay. India take on Sri Lanka in the Women's Asia Cup final in Dubai on Sunday.

Article Title: 'He shouldn't be here': Nasser Hussain bashes Pakistan with Virender Sehwag example

Former England captain Nasser Hussain has slammed Pakistan’s decision to bring Saim Ayub into the Test team straight from the Caribbean Premier League (CPL), saying the young batter “shouldn't be here”.Ayub’s return to the Pakistan Test team ended in a nightmare as he was dismissed for a duck in both innings of the third Test against England at Edgbaston. The young opener faced only 11 balls across the two innings, with England pacer Ollie Robinson dismissing him on both occasions.Ayub had arrived in England after playing T20 cricket in the CPL. Hussain questioned why Pakistan chose to bring him into a Test match without enough preparation for the conditions.Speaking on Sky Sports after Pakistan finished Day 2 at 52-2 in their second innings, Hussain said Ayub should not have been picked for the Test.“The truth is he shouldn't be here. He came from the CPL and hasn't played first-class cricket in some time,” Hussain said during a post-day show on Sky Sports.Hussain said bringing a player directly from T20 cricket into a Test in England was a poor decision.“I don't know who thinks it's the right thing to fly someone over from foreign conditions, playing a completely different format, and think they're going to be fine in these conditions against a Dukes ball, against Ollie Robinson and England's bowling attack,” Hussain asserted, explaining why Ayub was destined to fail in these conditions against a team of the calibre of England.Hussain also recalled what happened when India once took a similar approach with Virender Sehwag Sehwag was flown into England without enough match practice and struggled at the same ground. Hussain said that if even a player of Sehwag’s experience could struggle, Pakistan should not have expected Ayub to immediately succeed.“Virender Sehwag tried it on this ground, if you remember... they flew him in. Virender Sehwag got a pair, and that's Virender Sehwag, who's a better, more experienced player than Saim,” highlighted Hussain.Hussain said Ayub must take some responsibility for the shot he played, but he questioned the decision-makers who selected him.“So a bit of responsibility goes to the lad for the shot he played. But also, whoever thought that was a seriously good decision and that he was going to go okay this week?”“It is just a sort of disrespect and disregard for Test match cricket. Test match cricket, as any cricketer will tell you, is the toughest format. Batting at the top of the order in England is the toughest task, and you just feel you can fly someone in from some part of the world and go, Good luck,” he said.
Article Summary: Saim Ayub was dismissed for a duck in both innings of the third Test against England at Edgbaston. The young opener faced only 11 balls across the two innings, with England pacer Ollie Robinson dismissing him on both occasions. Hussain questioned why Pakistan chose to bring him into a Test match without enough preparation for the conditions.

Article Title: Ranji Trophy: Brabourne Stadium to be Railways home venue in 2026-27 season
Article Text:

MUMBAI: In a first, the iconic Brabourne Stadium at the Cricket Club of India here will be the home venue of Railways in the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy In the past, the Railways have played their home Ranji Trophy matches at the Karnail Singh Stadium in New Delhi.Placed in Elite Group D, Railways will play their three 2026-27 Ranji Trophy home ties at the Brabourne Stadium-their season-the opening match against Uttarakhand from Oct 11-14, the big game against 42-time champions Mumbai (it will be an away game for Mumbai!) from Nov 2-5, and then against Haryana from Jan 17-20.This will be the first time the Brabourne Stadium will stage a Ranji Trophy match in more than three years. The historic venue last staged a Ranji Trophy match between Mumbai and Maharashtra from Jan 24-27, 2023. The match ended in a draw."I'm truly happy that the Ranji Trophy is returning to the CCI. The Brabourne Stadium has staged the maximum number of Ranji Trophy finals (16) in India. There's a replica of the Ranji Trophy in the CCI main hall, which was kept by former BCCI and CCI president Raj Singh Dungarpur many years back.So, there has always been a special and cherished relationship between Brabourne stadium CCI's senior member and well-known cricket lover Sachin Bajaj told TOI on Saturday."My old friend Syed Zakaria Zuffri (former Assam and Railways ‘keeper-batsman and current Railways head coach) requested to me if the CCI could stage Railways' home Ranji Trophy matches in the upcoming season. I asked him to contact CCI's Cricket committee vice-chairman Mayank Khandwala in this regard. I must appreciate the efforts of Mayank and the CCI cricket committee in making this happen," he added."It is a matter of immense pride and great emotion for all of us at the Cricket Club of India to welcome the Ranji Trophy back to Brabourne Stadium after a significant interval. Cricket at CCI is not merely a sport, it is part of the Club’s identity, its heritage and its soul. For generations, Brabourne Stadium has witnessed some of the finest moments in Indian cricket and has been privileged to host legendary players, great teams and memorable encounters. The Ranji Trophy has always held a very special place in that extraordinary history. The return of first-class cricket to CCI is therefore much more than the staging of a few matches. It is the revival of a proud cricketing tradition and the reopening of a historic chapter. We are particularly delighted that Railways have chosen CCI as their home ground. We are honoured to partner with them and are committed to providing the players, officials and spectators with the very best facilities and an environment befitting the stature of the Ranji Trophy," Khandwala told TOI."As the vice-chairman of the Cricket Committee at CCI, I believe strongly that our responsibility is not only to preserve the magnificent cricketing legacy of this institution, but also to keep that legacy alive for the next generation. Bringing premier domestic cricket back to Brabourne is an important part of that vision. The Ranji Trophy represents the foundation of Indian cricket. It is where talent is tested, characters are built and future international stars begin their journey. To have that journey once again unfolding at CCI is something we should all celebrate. The Brabourne Stadium has a history that speaks for itself. Now, we look forward to creating the next chapter. On behalf of CCI, we extend a warm welcome to Railways, the players, support staff, match officials, the BCCI and, most importantly, cricket lovers who will return to CCI to experience the magic of first-class cricket. The Ranji Trophy is coming home to CCI. The heritage continues, and the next chapter begins," he added.The Railways team playing its home ties in the Ranji Trophy in the upcoming season is another step forward in cricket returning to CCI. Earlier this month, the International Cricket Council had announced that India will stage the inaugural edition of the six-team inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy 2027, with matches scheduled between 14-28 Feb, 2027 at the Brabourne Stadium in Mumbai and the Kotambi Stadium Vadodara.It’s learnt that the CCI is currently installing new floodlights at the Brabourne Stadium. “We are in the process of installing new floodlights at the stadium. We’ll commission the new lights by Oct 10-15,” Khandwala said.The Railways have clinched the coveted Ranji Trophy twice in the past -in 2001–02 and 2004–05. However, they've met with little success in recent years, and failed to move beyond the league stage of the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy, finishing fourth in Elite Group C with 23 points in seven matches.
Article Summary: The iconic Brabourne Stadium at the Cricket Club of India will be the home venue of Railways in the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy. The historic venue last staged a Ranji trophy match between Mumbai and Maharashtra from Jan 24-27, 2023.

Chennai: Tilak Varma was finally dismissed in this year’s Duleep Trophy, falling agonisingly short of a second century. Despite being dismissed for 99, the South Zone captain’s red-ball ambitions stay intact, even though his team is staring at a big loss against East at the MA Chidambaram Stadium.Tilak, who had scored a century and a half-century in South Zone’s semifinal win against North Zone without being dismissed, battled through the Chennai heat on Wednesday against a quality East Zone attack. He was the last man to fall, giving a return catch to off-spinner Kounain Quraishi, as South were eventually bowled out for 336, conceding a massive 372-run first-innings lead.East, opting to bat again rather than send their bowlers back out, were 212-5 at stumps on Day Four, stretching their lead to 584.For Tilak, however, the larger picture remained clear. England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum has asked newly appointed mentor Kevin Pietersen to challenge the team’s setup and speak up with ideas that could help improve the side.Pietersen was appointed last week and joined England’s coaching staff ahead of the T20 series against Sri Lanka. Article Title: 'Will get both our trophies back,' asserts BCCI after not accepting silverware from ACC chief Mohsin Naqvi

MUMBAI: A familiar script has repeated itself. And ironically, at the same venue - the Dubai International Cricket Stadium. Almost 12 months after Suryakumar Yadav's victorious Indian team came home without the Asia Cup Trophy, refusing to accept it from Mohsin Naqvi, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman, who is currently heading the Asian Cricket Council (ACC) and Pakistan's interior minister, Harmanpreet Kaur & Co did an encore after clinching the 2026 Women's Asia Cup in Dubai, shunning the trophy ceremony on Sunday night due to the presence of Naqvi on the stage.Like in case of the men's team, the women's team too returned home empty - despite triumphing in the Asia Cup women's championship in style, winning all their five matches, including recording a thumping 72-run win over Sri Lanka in a one-sided final on Sunday.Naqvi showed up at the stadium minutes before the last ball was bowled and insisted on presenting the winners' trophy himself, despite being told by the BCCI authorities clearly that the Indian women's team would not accept the trophy from him. It was a repeat show of what the Indian men's team did on September 28 last year. The brief and delayed presentation ceremony eventually concluded without the winners receiving their prize.There were behind-the-scenes discussions over the post-match formalities, with the BCCI proposing that ACC vice-president Khalid Al Zarooni could present the trophy. However, Naqvi did not relent. He stood on the podium and handed the runners-up cheque to the Sri Lankan team.Al Zarooni, Sri Lanka Cricket Transformation Committee head Eran Wickramaratne, Emirates Cricket Board (ECB) secretary general Mubashir Usmani and a female representative of DP World, the title sponsor of the Asia Cup, were among those on the podium.BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia and vice-president Rajeev Shukla were present in the stadium but they did not go up on the dais or share the stage with Naqvi. There were visuals of Saikia and Shukla speaking cordially with Naqvi in the Royal Box that went viral. They spoke to Team Indian on the ground, presented them medals and congratulated them on their record-extending eighth Asia Cup title. "At some point, we would get both our Asia Cup trophies back," Saikia asserted, while talking to TOI from Dubai.Explaining India's uncompromising stand regarding not receiving the trophy from Naqvi, Saikia told this paper, "We had taken a conscious decision considering all prevailing aspects, and our position had been communicated to the ACC in advance, that the Indian team would not participate in the trophy presentation under the circumstances.Our participation in the Asia Cup was in fulfilment of our sporting commitments as a member of the Asian Cricket Council by adhering to the policy in place, and there was never any question of compromising on the spirit of the game or our commitment to international cricket.However, participation in a multinational tournament and the manner in which the trophy is presented or received are two separate and distinct issues.
Article Summary: India won the 2026 Women's Asia Cup in Dubai on Sunday. But they did not accept the trophy from Mohsin Naqvi, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman. It was a repeat show of what the Indian men's team did on September 28 last year.

Article Title: ‘You don’t treat human beings that way’: Michael Holding slams Pakistan over Imran Khan’s treatment
Article Text:
Michael Holding and Imran Khan (Agency Image)

Michael Holding speaks out for Imran Khan

'You don't treat human beings that way'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former West Indies pacer Michael Holding has joined the growing list of cricketing figures calling for better treatment of former Pakistan captain Imran Khan , saying the imprisoned 1992 World Cup winner should be treated “just like another human being”.Imran has been in a Pakistani prison since 2023 while facing ongoing legal cases, with concerns over his health and access to basic facilities continuing to grow. His family has claimed that he does not even have access to books and has not been provided proper medical facilities.The issue gained fresh attention after 21 international captains including Sunil Gavaskar and Kapil Dev, wrote to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif , urging authorities to ensure basic amenities for Imran. Pat Cummins , Wasim Akram, Javed Miandad and Brian Lara also subsequently spoke in support of humane treatment for the former Pakistan all-rounder.Holding, who played alongside and against Imran during their international careers, said the situation involving the former Pakistan captain was deeply upsetting.“I'll mention one name, Imran Khan, but you probably don't want to go down the political route, and I don't want to either, but that's a sad story. become one of the former Pakistan captain’s defining legacies. I played with Imran, I wouldn't say I played a lot.I played some one-day games with him. I played county cricket, a few games against Imran, but apart from playing with Imran, I have spent time with Imran,” Holding told Sports Now.The former fast bowler recalled his association with Imran away from cricket as well. He remembered accompanying him in London when the former Pakistan captain was raising funds for his cancer hospital."When Imran was going around London looking to garner funds for that cancer hospital, I went around with him, I tried to support him as best as I possibly could, where that was concerned. So I know the man, and I know exactly what type of person that he is. And it's extremely sad to see the situation now and what is going on with Imran Khan," the 72-year-old recalled.Holding's comments came after the appeal from former international captains seeking proper medical care and family access for Imran. The West Indies great backed that demand while stressing that the issue should not be viewed simply through the prism of politics.Holding said he fully supported the captains who had written to the Pakistan Prime Minister and questioned why Imran should be treated differently from other prisoners."I am in total support of the captains who wrote that letter. I don't know what effect it will have, but I am in total support of trying to get the man to be treated just like another human being. You don't treat human beings that way. People who have committed murder aren't treated that way.So I don't see the reason why this man should be treated that way," Holding said.He also questioned whether jealousy could be a factor, pointing to Imran's extraordinary global profile.“I don't know if there's jealousy involved in this, because Imran Khan. I don't think there's a Pakistani that is more well known around the world than Imran Khan. That is ridiculous, the way the man is being treated,” he added.The controversy surrounding Imran's prison conditions had already spilled into the cricketing world after Michael Atherton interviewed his sons, Sulaiman and Kasim, on the sidelines of the Lord's Test between England and Pakistan. The PCB subsequently threatened to pull out of the fixture, but Sky Sports went ahead and broadcast the 18-minute interview.In the interview, Imran's sons alleged that their father was being denied proper medical facilities. Holding's intervention has now added another prominent voice to the calls for humane treatment of the former Pakistan captain.
Article Summary: Michael Holding says Imran Khan should be treated 'just like another human being' Former West Indies fast bowler adds his voice to calls for better treatment of former Pakistan captain. Imran has been in a Pakistani prison since 2023 while facing ongoing legal cases. His family has claimed that he does not even have access to books.

Article Title: Sunil Gavaskar urges BCCI to make big change, names Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid for key role

Sunil Gavaskar believes the BCCI needs to rethink the role of its Cricket Advisory Committee (CAC), suggesting that the panel should have a far wider mandate and draw on the experience of some of India's most celebrated former cricketers.The former India captain's call comes after he criticised East Zone's approach in the Duleep Trophy final, where Ishan Kishan's side settled for the title on the basis of a first-innings lead. Gavaskar has previously expressed his dissatisfaction with the rule, which has continued to attract criticism over several domestic seasons.According to Gavaskar, the CAC could play a much larger role in addressing such issues and shaping the future of Indian cricket.The current CAC appointments date back to 2022, when Ashok Malhotra, Jatin Paranjape and Sulakshana Naik were named to the three-member panel. Its traditional responsibilities have centred on selecting the head coach and national selectors, with the committee also conducting interviews for those positions.However, there is uncertainty over whether the CAC still exists in its current form or has been disbanded.Gavaskar believes the BCCI should instead broaden the committee's remit to cover wider aspects of the game, including domestic and international scheduling."There are no longer any committees in BCCI today apart from the selection committees and the CAC. Perhaps the time has come to expand the CAC and its brief of selecting the selectors and coach, and also look at fixtures — domestic and international, and all things related to Indian cricket. There are some incredibly experienced former cricketers whose expertise can be utilised to be on this committee," Gavaskar wrote in his column for the Mid-Day.He also suggested a star-studded list of former India players who could contribute to such a panel."How about names like Sachin Tendulkar, Rahul Dravid, Sourav Ganguly, Ravi Shastri, Anil Kumble, Harbhajan Singh, Virender Sehwag — to name a few? The President and Secretary will be there too," he added.Gavaskar believes involving former greats such as Tendulkar and Dravid in discussions with India's coaching and development setup could bring an additional level of expertise and authority."When this committee interacts with the coach and captain and the head of the NCA, it carries a heft beyond measure. A similar committee for women’s cricket, too, where experience and expertise meet to take calls to take Indian cricket forward," wrote Gavaskar.The former batter, who also captained India to the 1985 Championship win, wants the idea to extend beyond the men's game, with a comparable advisory structure for women's cricket."Just thinking about this gives one the goosebumps. Will it ever happen, or is it just a dream?" he concluded.

Article Title: 'Are they living in the past?': Ex-India cricketer slams Mohsin Naqvi after Asia Cup trophy snub
Article Text:
Mohsin Naqvi

Mohammad Kaif questions Naqvi's dual responsibilities

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's Women's Asia Cup triumph in Dubai was overshadowed by another awkward trophy presentation involving Asian Cricket Council president Mohsin Naqvi, as the champions once again declined to collect the silverware from the Pakistan Cricket Board chief.India defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final on Sunday to claim the title, but the post-match ceremony was held up amid the standoff. Naqvi, who is also Pakistan 's Interior Minister, remained at the venue, but India's players were unwilling to receive the trophy from him.The episode was strikingly similar to last year's men's Asia Cup final, when India's victorious team had also refused to accept the trophy from Naqvi. The repeat has once again put the spotlight on his dual role as a senior cricket administrator and a prominent figure in Pakistan's government.Former India batter Mohammad Kaif has questioned whether Naqvi can give sufficient attention to cricket administration while simultaneously handling major political responsibilities.“Are they living in the past? Don't they have a reality check? Mohsin Naqvi is in politics. He is the boss of the board. It's not like that,” Kaif said on Cricbuzz.“If you are in cricket, then you have to be in cricket. You have to go to two places.It's a difficult job. You won't be able to give time. You have so many political commitments. You have to run the cricket board. You have to see what's going on inside. You have to stop at one place and invest time. If you look at any body, if you compare it with the BCCI, or look at it from the outside, nobody does two things.”Naqvi's responsibilities extend beyond the PCB. As ACC president, PCB chairman and Pakistan's Interior Minister, he occupies influential positions across both cricket and government, making his involvement in major India-Pakistan cricket events particularly sensitive.Kaif believes leading a cricket board demands a level of focus that can be difficult to provide while holding another major office.“Either you are a politician, or you are a cricketer. You have to balance it. You have to focus on one thing,” he said.Kaif also rejected the idea that Pakistan's cricketing problems stem from a lack of talented players.According to the former India international, Pakistan continues to possess considerable natural ability but needs a better system and the right people to turn that talent into successful professional cricketers.“Players aren't bad. You need people who make players. There is a lot of talent in Pakistan,” he added.The latest controversy has ensured that India's Women's Asia Cup victory will be remembered for more than the 72-run win over Sri Lanka. Instead of a routine trophy celebration, the final once again ended with an unresolved presentation involving Naqvi.With a similar situation having played out at the men's Asia Cup final last year, questions over Naqvi's role at the intersection of cricket administration and politics are likely to remain part of the conversation.
Article Summary: Mohammad Kaif questions whether Mohsin Naqvi can give enough attention to cricket administration while handling major political responsibilities. India's Women's Asia Cup triumph in Dubai was overshadowed by another awkward trophy presentation involving the Pakistan Cricket Board chief. India defeated Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final on Sunday to claim the title.

Article Title: Rajasthan stuck in 2012, Manipur in 2023: How actively are states with CWG medals promoting sports?
Article Text:
Are sports bodies of Indian states promoting the game properly?

Medal tally of India's athletes by birth state/UT

Haryana: Hit on the podium, not so much off it

Manipur still talking about 2023

Rajasthan: 14 years and counting

Uttar Pradesh and Delhi carry the same gloomy picture

And then come Tamil Nadu and others

The ones somewhere in the middle

How active are states/UTs with CWG medallists in promoting sport

Does it matter so much?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Social media presence Local sports events Government funding 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Somewhere on a muddy school field in Haryana right now, a teenager is perhaps drilling the same throwing technique over and over, just as she had watched on television just days ago. Her sole aim is to pull off the one like Sharmila Dhankar, India's Commonwealth Games shot put gold medallist.Before the 2026 CWG campaign, she, like many of us, had almost certainly never heard the name. And it's not because Dhankar had not won anything before the Glasgow Games; she had, a gold medal in the Women's Shot Put F57 event at the 2026 Fazza International Para Athletics Championship, but because one of the primary institutions whose entire job was to carry that story back from the medal podium to villages and training grounds across the state has, for all practical purposes, gone quiet.That's the part of this story that rarely gets told. India walked away from Glasgow with 39 medals, and for a week, the athletes who won them were everywhere, garlanded at airports, seated beside ministers, their faces on the evening news. But medals don't build the next generation of athletes by themselves. Somebody has to keep telling their stories, long after the felicitation photo is filed away, to the kid training in a dusty school ground who needs proof that this path actually leads somewhere.We wanted to know which state sports departments are still doing their job of promoting the sports and their grassroots on their social media platforms, and which ones seem to have simply logged off. So we scrolled through the timelines ourselves. Here's what we found.No state produced more glory in Glasgow than Haryana. Eleven medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze, spanning boxing, wrestling, athletics, and para sport, headlined by a Neeraj Chopra silver that will be replayed on sports channels for years.Alongside him were names most of India still had little knowledge of. The likes of Preeti Pawar, Jaismine Lamboria, Sakshi Chaudhary, Priya Ghanghas, Sachin Siwach, and Ankush Panghal, all of whom trained in government facilities, under government schemes, and who'd probably appreciate their own state department cheering as loudly for them as it does for its concert lineups.Because that's the thing. The Sports Department, Government of Haryana's X account has posted exactly once in all of 2026, and it's a flyer for the music acts playing at the Chief Minister's Cup.Facebook and Instagram follow a similar rhythm with a short cluster of posts around that February event, and then not much else.Eleven medals, and not one dedicated post to show for it. Somewhere in Rohtak or Bhiwani, a young pugilist training in Priya Ghanghas's discipline would probably just like a little proof that someone up top is paying attention.Manipur's page has an odd time-capsule quality to it. This is the state that gave India Mirabai Chanu, one of the country's most beloved Olympic medalists, and this Commonwealth Games alone produced four medalists from Manipur, Chanu's gold among them, alongside Rishikanta Singh, Bindyarani Devi, and Jadumani Singh.And yet the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports' X account hasn't posted since October 2023, a "Run for Unity" event, frozen well before any of this year's medals happened.Although the Facebook page has had a few sporadic posts here and there this year, its Instagram account has managed just two posts since January. It’s the kind of gap that makes you wonder if someone simply forgot the login details somewhere along the way.If there's one number in this whole exercise worth sitting with, it's this: the official Sports Department, Government of Rajasthan hasn't posted on Facebook since April 14, 2012.Fourteen years, through Arundhati Choudhary's Commonwealth gold and everything else that's happened in Rajasthan sport since.Its X account's last original post predates a retweet from March 2021, and there's no Instagram at all. A parallel handle, the Rajasthan State Sports Council, exists across all three platforms and is barely livelier.Somewhere behind Choudhary's medal is a genuinely good story, but it just hasn't found a home on the one page built to tell it.Gulveer Singh managed both a silver and a bronze for Uttar Pradesh this Games, a rare double that would make a great centrepiece for the state's sporting year. Instead, across two separate official handles on three platforms, Uttar Pradesh Sports has produced little beyond reposts, while its sister account, Sports Directorate, Govt of Uttar Pradesh, hasn't posted at all in 2026.Delhi Government, for its part, doesn't run a dedicated sports account at all on any of the popular social media platforms, so gold medalist Harsh Singh and bronze medalist Tejaswin Shankar, both representing India's capital, don't really have an institutional cheerleader online, their wins quietly absorbed into the general churn of city government updates. Both athletes are, in effect, doing their own promotional legwork.Set against all that quiet, Tamil Nadu feels like a different sport altogether. Its Sports Tamil Nadu handles post multiple times a day, celebrating not just its own three medalists, Praveen Chithravel, Selva Prabhu, Muthupandi Raja, but athletes from other states too, weaving in government scheme updates without it ever reading like bureaucracy.Every medallist got a dedicated post. Somewhere in Tamil Nadu, a kid training in long jump or wrestling doesn't have to wonder whether the sport leads anywhere. The state tells them, publicly, almost daily.Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka's Facebook and Instagram pages, Assam, Bihar, and Tripura all follow a version of that same habit, active, consistent, generous with attention toward athletes nobody outside their district would otherwise know existed.Kerala doesn't run a separate sports handle on X but keeps its Facebook and Instagram genuinely lively, making sure Murali Sreeshankar and Mohammed Basil's silvers got their due.Andhra Pradesh mirrors that same rhythm across all three platforms.Not every state falls neatly into being inactive or staying proactive. Punjab's account managed just two posts on X all year, New Year's and Republic Day, though its Facebook and Instagram carry a bit more life around coaching and departmental meetings, even if athletes rarely get top billing.Uttarakhand was genuinely active last year before cooling off in 2026, leaning more toward government scheme announcements on Facebook, though its Instagram at least carried two posts around the Games.Maharashtra has dedicated posts up for both Sarvesh Kushare and Dilip Gavit, with Instagram staying fairly regular, enough effort to stay out of the quiet column.Karnataka's X account hasn't posted since March 2024, around an unrelated cultural-team event, even though its Facebook and Instagram have stayed warm and active toward its CWG medalists.It is worth asking why this actually matters, beyond good manners. Well, a state sports department's social media feed isn't just a courtesy board for congratulations; it's one of the cheapest, most direct tools available to build the next generation of athletes.A youngster in a small town is far more likely to pick up a javelin because they saw a state government post celebrating someone from their own district. Even when it comes to promoting any government policy, social media can be as effective.Visibility drives aspiration. There's a funding logic too. Sponsors, corporates, and even state finance departments allocate resources partly based on visible public interest, and a well-run social account is often the easiest evidence a sport has that interest.ALSO READ: Anahat Singh: What is in the name? A word from Guru Nanak's prayer, now India's squash sensation Silence, on the other hand, sends the message that grassroots sport isn't a priority worth the effort of a single post, even when the state has just produced a medallist on the world stage.It is worth it because sometimes, the first step towards building a sporting culture is simply showing people that their achievements are being seen.
Article Summary: India won 39 medals at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. Haryana produced 11 medallists, including seven gold, two silver, two bronze. But the state sports department has posted just once in all of 2026. What do you think is more important for grassroots sports promotion? Government funding or social media presence? Share your view.

Article Title: ‘That video was not ordinary’: PM Modi praises Lovlina for objecting to distorted India map - Watch
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi shares a light moment with boxer Lovlina Borgohain. (PTI Photo)

‘That video was not ordinary’

Mirabai opens up about four difficult years

Narender's joke leaves Modi laughing

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Boxer Lovlina Borgohain's decision to object to a distorted Indian map during the Commonwealth Games earned special appreciation from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time.Lovlina, who won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow, was among India's medal winners who interacted with Modi at his residence on Sunday. The meeting, attended by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Minister of State for Sports Raksha Khadse and Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha, saw athletes recount their experiences from the Games in an informal and emotional setting.In a little over 10-minute video of the interaction shared by the Prime Minister's Office on Monday, Modi brought up Lovlina's confrontation with a restaurant in Glasgow after she noticed a distorted Indian map.“Kya hua wo restaurant waale se jhagda kar rahi thi? (What happened, you were fighting with that restaurant guy?)” Modi asked.Lovlina laughed before explaining why she intervened.“We had such a good performance and it was the last day of the Games. It was a happy occasion sir, we were celebrating and I didn't like it when I saw the distorted map. I politely told them and they have made the changes also,” she explained.Modi applauded the boxer for noticing the issue despite being in the middle of celebrations after her medal-winning campaign.“To be able to recognise the significance of that map at a time when you were celebrating and the Games were over, I can tell you truthfully, that video was not ordinary. It will be remembered by people for a very long time,” he told the Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist.India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.The interaction also provided an emotional window into Mirabai Chanu's journey to her gold medal in the women's 48kg category. The weightlifter produced a Games-record lift of 190kg, but her triumph came after four difficult years following her one-kilogram miss at the Paris Olympics. Modi asked Mirabai about the tears she shed on the podium and even fed her a laddu during their interaction.“Itne aansu tapak rahe the (So many tears were rolling down),” Modi remarked.Mirabai explained that the tears represented years of accumulated emotions.“I was very happy and emotional at that moment. I was crying because I missed a medal in the Paris Olympics by one kilogram. I have faced a lot in these last four years. I was battling injuries and some family problems too.“There were a lot of things. So, these four years were very tough for me. And when I stood on the podium, our flag went up and the anthem played, it was hard to stop myself,” she said.The meeting also had its lighter moments. Boxer Narender Berwal, who won silver in the +90kg category, recalled a funny exchange with a Pakistani boxer after beating him at the 2015 World Military Games.“During the 2015 World Military Games, I had a bout with a Pakistani boxer. I won it but when we were together in the medical room for treatment to our niggles, he said to me 'Bhaijan aapka naam Narender hai, aapke coach ka naam Narender hai, aapke Pradhan Mantri ka naam Narender hai, mujhe Narender naam se nafrat ho gayi hai.' (Brother, you, your coach and your PM are all named Narender. I hate this name now),” he recalled, drawing laughter from Modi.The Prime Minister also underlined the broader significance of the athletes' achievements, saying their medals were helping inspire a new generation.“I have been in this house for 12-13 years now and if there is one group that I have met regularly here, it is the athletes because of your efforts to win medals for India and your tradition of scaling new heights.“Far more than our push to promote sports in schools, it is your medals that inspire people,” Modi said.
Article Summary: Lovlina Borgohain won silver in the women's 75kg category in Glasgow. Prime Minister Narendra Modi described the moment as one that would be remembered for a long time. India finished fourth in Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 golds, with boxing contributing seven gold medals.

Article Text:

I feel as if from every drop of tears, gold medals are dripping,” Modi told the Olympic silver medallist.Mirabai, who won gold in Glasgow, opened up about the difficult journey that preceded her Commonwealth Games triumph, including the disappointment of the Paris Olympics.“I was very happy, and emotional too. That day the happiness was greater and I cried because at the Paris Olympics, I lost a medal by 1 kg. In a player’s life what all we have to face. So within these 4 years, how much and what all I had faced, every time injuries were going on and all that was happening.So with great difficulty I had faced these 4 years. So when all that happened, on the podium when I stood, sir, and when our flag goes up and our national anthem plays, sir, we cannot stop, sir, tears come out on their own,” she said.Modi responded by highlighting the wider impact of the athletes' achievements.“This is very good. It is not as if this achievement of yours is considered only your achievement; your victory becomes a very big inspiration for the coming generations.”The informal interaction also saw athletes share lighter and deeply personal moments from their Glasgow campaigns.Modi reminded para shot put gold medallist Sharmila Dhankar of a promise she had made earlier.“You made a promise. Last time, yours, both daughters will become players,” Modi said with a smile.Dhankar replied: “Haanji, right now they are young in age. In the next Commonwealth, one family will bring 3 medals.”Men's 100m T47 gold medallist Dilip Gavit, meanwhile, spoke about dedicating his performance to his guru.“When I was running, when my event was on 29th (July), that day was Guru Purnima, so that day I gave a gift to my guru,” he was heard saying in the video.In another video posted by Modi, gold medallist boxer Sakshi Chaudhary introduced herself and the contingent.“Hello friends! This is Sakshi Chaudhary. Today, our honourable Prime Minister has invited us, the Commonwealth Games medalists, and we feel very proud. We are extremely happy to have met him; he is very humble. Sir, would you like to say something?” she said.Modi replied with a message that summed up his interaction with the athletes: “Jo khelega, woh khilega” (The one who plays, will blossom). “Always cheer for Bharat.”India's fourth-place finish came despite a significantly smaller contingent and a reduced sporting programme compared to Birmingham 2022. India sent 122 athletes to Glasgow, compared to 210 in Birmingham, while 30 of its 61 medals in 2022 came in sports that were not part of the Glasgow programme.Despite those limitations, India retained its fourth-place position and improved its medal conversion rate, with 38 athletes returning home with medals. Long-distance runner Gulveer Singh was the only Indian athlete to win two medals.The Glasgow Games concluded after 11 days, with Scotland handing over the Commonwealth Games flag and ceremonial baton to India ahead of the 2030 edition in Ahmedabad.The symbols were handed to Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra, Indian Olympic Association president PT Usha and Gujarat Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi during the closing ceremony.Ahmedabad will become only the second Indian city to host the Commonwealth Games after New Delhi staged the 2010 edition.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi hosted medal-winning contingent at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg. Modi heard athletes recount some of the moments that defined their journeys. India returned from Glasgow with 39 medals, including 13 gold, 17 silver and nine bronze.
